sources.title: Foreign Ministry: current tourist visa Group I/II/III framework

It repeats the current Group I/II/III tourist framework, including Group III prior DIGEMIG consultation and its required authorization resolution.

sources.title: Supreme Decree 4828: current tourist/visit visas and entry authorizations

sources.supportingExcerpt: Países Grupo II: Las personas extranjeras pertenecientes al Grupo II de países requieren visa de turismo o visita, o autorización de ingreso.

sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry's official notice says the bilateral visa-exemption agreement became effective on 11 November 2021 for tourism or visits.

policies.title: Bolivian ordinary passport: citizenship/home entry
policies.summary: Article 21 of the current Constitution gives Bolivians freedom of residence, permanence and movement in Bolivian territory, expressly including entry into the country. This supports the home/citizenship normalization.
conditions: This is a Bolivian ordinary-passport citizenship/home-entry normalization, not a visitor-visa, residence, dual-nationality, emergency-document, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless or other special-document rule.
Migration registration/control and lawful identity or travel-document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Group I ordinary passports: visa-free tourism or visit
policies.summary: The live Ministry country API assigns 54 mapped catalog nationalities to Group I. Later official measures override stale API rows for Honduras, Israel, El Salvador, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; the resulting 58 named ordinary passports are visa-free for tourism or visits.
conditions: The scope is tourism or visit only, without a residence purpose. The source does not establish a nationality-wide ETA, eVisa, or visa-on-arrival requirement for this group.

Honduras follows the bilateral tourist/visit visa suppression effective 17 March 2024; El Salvador the ordinary-passport agreement effective 21 June 2024; the Dominican Republic its waiver effective 2 September 2024; and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines its agreement effective 11 November 2021.

The 1 December 2025 announcement controls South Korea, South Africa, Bulgaria, Malta, Romania, United Arab Emirates, Israel and United States. The API has not updated Israel and is not followed for that older Group III value.

Passport/document validity, identity, admission screening, health evidence where applicable, stay, purpose, extension and other migration conditions remain outside this nationality baseline. Diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless and other special documents are excluded.

policies.title: Group II ordinary passports: tourist/visit visa or qualifying entry authorization
policies.summary: The current Ministry country API assigns these 100 unambiguously mapped catalog nationalities to Group II. Current law requires a tourism/visit visa or a DIGEMIG tourist/visit entry authorization. Neither route is an electronically issued visa or an unconditional passport-wide visa on arrival.
conditions: Current law requires a Group II tourism/visit visa or a DIGEMIG tourist/visit entry authorization. The official portal is an application system, while the Ministry describes the visa itself as issued by consulates and embassies; neither source establishes electronic visa issuance.

DIGEMIG may issue the alternate authorization at a land or airport border, or exceptionally at an office, when the traveller could not access a Bolivian mission. It requires the same evidence and procedures as a visa and is not an unconditional nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route.

Applicants must meet the Ministry’s stated requirements, including ordinarily a valid passport, application declaration, itinerary/return travel, invitation or accommodation, means, photograph and yellow-fever evidence where applicable. Admission remains subject to control.
No residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, special-document or third-country-document route is normalized.

policies.title: Group III ordinary passports: tourist/visit visa with prior DIGEMIG verification
policies.summary: The current Ministry country API assigns these 18 unambiguously mapped catalog nationalities to Group III. The current framework requires a tourism/visit visa after verification and authorization by DIGEMIG; the duplicate contradictory Libya records are left unresolved.
conditions: This is a visa requirement with prior Group III verification and authorization by DIGEMIG. A border-issued authorization is possible only exceptionally after reasoned DIGEMIG authorization, so it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route and is not normalized as eVisa or ETA.
The Ministry’s electronic service accepts visa applications, but reviewed sources establish consular issuance and do not establish electronic issuance of the visa or electronic permission to board.

The general tourism/visit application requirements and final border-admission control apply. Residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, special-document and third-country-document rules are excluded.
